title: Space Tourism: Hong Kong deep edition

questions.q: In "Read your local market Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Close to the wider region: many small firms serve customers across the border, so shipping and data rules matter early. Check with a local expert.
Choose sole trader, partnership or company: a company separates personal and business risk, but has yearly filing duties. Check with a local expert.
Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit well; many one-person firms need flexible support.
Launch a pilot day with a go or no-go rule: 10 paid guests and zero safety incidents. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Choose your sector Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Trust: put the business registration number, a real address and a refund note on every page. Check with a local expert.
Local caution: A city with high costs: test one small offer before you sign a lease.
Compare three models: ground experience, agent for a licensed flight operator, content and training club. Pick by risk and margin.
Freelancers are common; write scope, price and date in one page before work starts.

questions.q: In "Register and license Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Contribution per unit = price minus the cost of each unit.
Choose sole trader, partnership or company: a company separates personal and business risk, but has yearly filing duties. Check with a local expert.
Cluster A, Online selling and marketing: Strong fit: customers shop on phones and expect delivery within a day. Compete on speed and service, not price.
Language: show both languages side by side; keep prices in HKD only.

questions.q: In "Protect data and customers Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Payments: bank transfer and fast-payment apps first; give an instant receipt.
A monthly review: what we planned, what happened, what we change.
Direct marketing needs a clear choice for the customer to say no; keep that record.
Launch a pilot day with a go or no-go rule: 10 paid guests and zero safety incidents. Check with a local expert.

questions.q: In "Find and serve customers Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Close to the wider region: many small firms serve customers across the border, so shipping and data rules matter early. Check with a local expert.
A dense, trade-led city. Space is costly, so online and shared-space models fit well.
Show proof of the ground experience: photos, guest comments with consent, partner licence page. Check with a local expert.
Employers usually pay a compulsory retirement-fund contribution for staff; budget it from the first hire.

questions.q: In "Price, tax and money Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep a registered address and a named contact; a shared-office address is common for a first year.
Price the package with partner cost, venue, guide and margin; state what is not included.
Say in plain words what you collect and why; give a way to see and correct it.
Assign roles: guide, safety lead (from the licensed partner), guest host; write a briefing sheet.

questions.q: In "People and partners Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Cluster H, People and business support: Coaching, coworking and outsourcing fit well; many one-person firms need flexible support.
Launch a pilot day with a go or no-go rule: 10 paid guests and zero safety incidents. Check with a local expert.
Written terms, rest days and paid leave follow the employment law; keep signed copies. Check with a local expert.
Check against a worse case: if sales are 25% lower, do you still cover costs?

questions.q: In "Launch plan and review Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Channels: messaging apps, social media and marketplaces are where customers already are.
Launch a pilot day with a go or no-go rule: 10 paid guests and zero safety incidents. Check with a local expert.
Break-even units = fixed monthly cost divided by contribution per unit; round up.
Partner with a college, training body or business chamber to find helpers and to practise.
